# Model and source

```{r model}
mod <- readModelDb("Bosnak_2026_levofloxacin")
ui <- rxode2::rxode(mod)
```

* Citation: `r ui$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1093/jac/dkag284> (open access, PMC13464500)
* Model: `Bosnak_2026_levofloxacin`

```{r description, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
cat(ui$description, "\n")
```

# Population

Bosnak 2026 is a prospective, single-centre case-control study at Hacettepe
University Hospitals (Ankara, Turkiye) of adults with acute leukaemia or
undergoing allogeneic haematopoietic stem cell transplantation who had an
absolute neutrophil count below 500 cells/mm^3 for at least a week and took
oral levofloxacin 750 mg once daily as febrile-neutropenia prophylaxis. One
hundred and twenty neutropenic episodes in 108 patients were enrolled (60
prophylaxis failures matched to 60 successes; Tables 1 and 2). Four plasma
samples (2, 4, 8 and 24 h after one 750 mg dose) were complete in 103 episodes
(60 successes, 43 failures), which form the population PK analysis set
(Supplementary Table S2): median age 58 years (IQR 34-68), 57.3% male, median
weight 66.6 kg (IQR 59.5-72.0), median Cockcroft-Gault creatinine clearance
94 mL/min (IQR 75-143) and median neutrophil count 70 cells/mm^3.

```{r population}
str(ui$population[c("n_subjects", "n_patients", "sex_female_pct",
                    "renal_function", "dose_range")])
```

# Source trace

Every value is also carried as an in-file comment next to its `ini()` entry in
`inst/modeldb/specificDrugs/Bosnak_2026_levofloxacin.R`.

| Model element | Value | Source location |
|---|---|---|
| Structure: one compartment, first-order absorption and elimination | -- | Results 'Population PK model'; Supplementary S2 `pkmodel(ka, V, Cl)` |
| `lka` (fixed) | log(1.12) 1/h | Table 3; Results (fixed to the preliminary estimate) |
| `lcl` | log(4.77) L/h | Table 3 CL/F |
| `lvc` | log(97.57) L | Table 3 V/F |
| `e_crcl_cl` | 0.81 | Table 3 'Effect of CRCL on CL/F'; equation CL/F = 4.77 x (CRCL/94)^0.81 |
| `e_wt_vc` (fixed) | 1 | Table 3 'Effect of WT on V/F'; equation V/F = 97.57 x (WT/66.6) |
| Covariate centring | WT 66.6 kg, CRCL 94 mL/min | Table 3 footnote; Supplementary S2 `log(WT/66.6)`, `log(CRCL/94)` |
| `etalcl` | log(0.4035^2 + 1) = 0.1508 | Table 3 IIV_CL/F 40.35 CV% |
| `etalvc` | log(0.3537^2 + 1) = 0.1179 | Table 3 IIV_V/F 35.37 CV% |
| `fu` (fixed) | 0.7 | Methods 'PK/PD target attainment' (30% binding); Supplementary S2 `Cfree = Cc * 0.7` |
| `propSd` | 0.25 | Table 3 proportional error 25.0 CV%; Supplementary S2 `proportional(b)` |

# Virtual cohort

The paper prints covariate distributions for the PK analysis set as a whole
(Supplementary Table S2) and, separately, for the prophylaxis-success and
prophylaxis-failure groups of the full 120-episode cohort (Tables 1 and 2).
Table 4 reports exposure by group, so two cohorts are built from the group
medians and interquartile ranges of age, body weight and serum creatinine,
with the group's female fraction; creatinine clearance is then computed from
each virtual patient by the Cockcroft-Gault equation on total body weight
(the paper does not state which weight it used). Each quantity is sampled
from a split distribution that reproduces its printed median and both
quartiles (log scale for weight and creatinine, linear for age).

```{r cohort}
# Split normal (or log-normal) through a printed median and IQR.
rsplit <- function(n, med, q1, q3, log = TRUE) {
  z <- stats::rnorm(n)
  if (log) {
    lo <- log(med / q1) / qnorm(0.75)
    hi <- log(q3 / med) / qnorm(0.75)
    exp(log(med) + ifelse(z < 0, lo, hi) * z)
  } else {
    lo <- (med - q1) / qnorm(0.75)
    hi <- (q3 - med) / qnorm(0.75)
    med + ifelse(z < 0, lo, hi) * z
  }
}

make_group <- function(group, n, age, wt, scr, pfemale) {
  d <- data.frame(
    group = group,
    AGE = pmin(pmax(rsplit(n, age[1], age[2], age[3], log = FALSE), 18), 90),
    WT = rsplit(n, wt[1], wt[2], wt[3]),
    SCR = rsplit(n, scr[1], scr[2], scr[3]),
    SEXF = stats::rbinom(n, 1, pfemale)
  )
  d$CRCL <- (140 - d$AGE) * d$WT / (72 * d$SCR) * ifelse(d$SEXF == 1, 0.85, 1)
  d
}

set.seed(2026)
n_per_group <- 150
cohort <- rbind(
  # Table 1 / Table 2 'Prophylaxis success' column
  make_group("Success", n_per_group, c(63.9, 33.3, 69.0), c(64.5, 60.0, 73.8),
             c(0.82, 0.67, 1.02), 0.650),
  # Table 1 / Table 2 'Prophylaxis failure' column
  make_group("Failure", n_per_group, c(52.0, 35.3, 64.0), c(67.5, 59.7, 74.5),
             c(0.72, 0.52, 0.89), 0.483)
)
cohort$id <- seq_len(nrow(cohort))

cohort_summary <- cohort |>
  summarise(
    across(c(WT, CRCL), list(
      median = median,
      q1 = ~ quantile(.x, 0.25),
      q3 = ~ quantile(.x, 0.75)
    ))
  )
knitr::kable(cohort_summary, digits = 1,
             caption = "Pooled virtual cohort; compare Supplementary Table S2 (WT 66.6 [59.5-72.0] kg, CRCL 94 [75-143] mL/min).")
```

The pooled cohort reproduces the PK-analysis covariate distribution of
Supplementary Table S2 closely, which is a check on both the Cockcroft-Gault
derivation and the group-level inputs.

```{r cohort-check}
stopifnot(
  abs(median(cohort$WT) / 66.6 - 1) < 0.05,
  abs(median(cohort$CRCL) / 94 - 1) < 0.15
)
```

# Simulation

Levofloxacin 750 mg once daily for seven days; the seventh dosing interval
(144-168 h) is at steady state (elimination half-life about 14 h at the
typical values).

```{r simulate}
dose_events <- rxode2::et(amt = 750, ii = 24, addl = 6, cmt = "depot") |>
  rxode2::et(c(0, seq(144, 168, by = 0.5)), cmt = "central") |>
  as.data.frame()

events <- merge(
  cohort[, c("id", "group", "WT", "CRCL")],
  dose_events[, setdiff(names(dose_events), "id")],
  by = NULL
) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))

rxode2::rxSetSeed(2026)
sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events, keep = "group", returnType = "data.frame")
```

## Typical-value profiles across renal function

Bosnak 2026 shows observed concentrations (Supplementary Figure S1) but no
model-predicted profiles; the figure below shows the model's typical steady-state
profile at the median weight for the Supplementary Table S2 quartiles of
creatinine clearance.

```{r typical-profiles}
# One single-subject solve per creatinine clearance, so that the
# typical-value (zeroRe) solve is not a multi-subject simulation.
mod_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)
typ <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(c(75, 94, 143)), function(i) {
  crcl <- c(75, 94, 143)[i]
  ev <- dose_events[, setdiff(names(dose_events), "id")]
  ev$WT <- 66.6
  ev$CRCL <- crcl
  out <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, ev, returnType = "data.frame")
  out$id <- i
  out$CRCL <- crcl
  out
}))

typ |>
  filter(time >= 144) |>
  mutate(tad = time - 144, CRCL = factor(paste(CRCL, "mL/min"),
                                         levels = paste(c(75, 94, 143), "mL/min"))) |>
  ggplot(aes(tad, Cc, colour = CRCL)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(x = "Time after dose (h)", y = "Total levofloxacin (mg/L)",
       colour = "CRCL",
       title = "Typical steady-state profiles, 750 mg once daily, WT 66.6 kg") +
  theme_minimal()
```

The steady-state unbound AUC0-24 of a typical patient has a closed form,
`fu * dose / (CL/F)`, so a PKNCA run on the typical solve must reproduce it.

```{r typical-closed-form}
typ_ss <- typ |> filter(time >= 144, id == 2)
typ_conc <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(typ_ss, Cu ~ time | id)
typ_int <- data.frame(start = 144, end = 168, auclast = TRUE)
typ_nca <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(typ_conc, intervals = typ_int))
typ_fauc <- as.data.frame(typ_nca)$PPORRES
c(pknca = typ_fauc, closed_form = 0.7 * 750 / 4.77)
stopifnot(abs(typ_fauc / (0.7 * 750 / 4.77) - 1) < 0.01)
```

# PKNCA validation

Steady-state Cmax, Cmin and AUC0-24 are computed with PKNCA over the 144-168 h
interval for each virtual patient, by group. Total concentrations (`Cc`) give
Cmax and Cmin; the unbound concentration (`Cu`) gives the unbound AUC0-24.

```{r pknca}
nca_input <- sim |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(id, group, time, Cc, Cu)

dose_df <- events |>
  filter(evid == 1) |>
  distinct(id, group) |>
  mutate(time = 0, amt = 750)

intervals_total <- data.frame(start = 144, end = 168, cmax = TRUE, cmin = TRUE)
intervals_free <- data.frame(start = 144, end = 168, auclast = TRUE)

nca_total <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(nca_input, Cc ~ time | group + id),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | group + id),
  intervals = intervals_total
))
nca_free <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(nca_input, Cu ~ time | group + id),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | group + id),
  intervals = intervals_free
))
nca_sim <- bind_rows(
  as.data.frame(nca_total$result),
  as.data.frame(nca_free$result)
)
```

## Comparison against Table 4

Table 4 of Bosnak 2026 gives the medians of the individual (Bayesian
posterior) exposures by prophylaxis group. Its "AUC0-24" row is the
**unbound** steady-state AUC0-24, not the total: the total steady-state
AUC of a typical patient is `750 / 4.77 = 157` mg*h/L, which no group median
in Table 4 approaches, while the unbound value `0.7 * 157 = 110` mg*h/L sits
between the two printed medians (108.3 and 90.67). This matches the fAUCtau
output of the authors' Monolix code. The Cmax and Cmin rows are total
concentrations (the assay measured total levofloxacin) at steady state; a
single 750 mg dose would give a typical Cmax near 6.7 mg/L, well below both
printed medians.

```{r nca-compare}
reference <- data.frame(
  group = c("Success", "Failure"),
  cmax = c(10.54, 9.46),     # Table 4 'Cmax (mg/L)'
  cmin = c(3.54, 2.43),      # Table 4 'Cmin (trough)'
  auclast = c(108.3, 90.67)  # Table 4 'AUC0-24' (unbound, steady state)
)
cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  nca_sim, reference,
  by = "group",
  units = c(cmax = "mg/L", cmin = "mg/L", auclast = "mg*h/L")
)
knitr::kable(
  cmp |> rename("Group" = group),
  caption = "Steady-state exposure medians: Table 4 of Bosnak 2026 against the simulation. Cmax and Cmin are total concentrations; the AUC row is the unbound AUC0-24."
)
```

```{r nca-footnote, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
if (!is.null(attr(cmp, "footnote"))) cat(attr(cmp, "footnote"), "\n")
```

Cmax and unbound AUC agree with Table 4 within about 10% in both groups, and
the simulated failure group has lower exposure than the success group, as in
the paper, because its younger patients with lower serum creatinine have
higher creatinine clearance. The simulated trough of the failure group runs
higher than its printed median. The trough is the exposure most sensitive to
the spread of the elimination rate, and the failure-group covariates are taken
from the full 60-episode group (Tables 1 and 2) rather than the 43 failures
that had complete PK sampling.

```{r nca-assert}
pct <- nca_sim |>
  group_by(group, PPTESTCD) |>
  summarise(sim = median(PPORRES), .groups = "drop") |>
  inner_join(
    reference |> pivot_longer(-group, names_to = "PPTESTCD", values_to = "ref"),
    by = c("group", "PPTESTCD")
  ) |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (sim / ref - 1))
stopifnot(
  # Structural: a mis-transcribed CL/F, V/F, dose or covariate centre moves
  # Cmax and AUC together by tens of percent.
  all(abs(pct$pct_diff[pct$PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "auclast")]) < 20),
  abs(median(pct$pct_diff)) < 10
)
```

# PK/PD target attainment

The paper's target is fAUC0-24/MIC >= 80, and its ROC analysis proposes an
exploratory prophylaxis cutoff of fAUC0-24/MIC >= 48.46. The figure shows the
fraction of the pooled virtual cohort reaching each target across MICs.

```{r pta}
fauc <- nca_sim |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast") |>
  select(id, group, fauc = PPORRES)

mics <- c(0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 6, 8, 12, 16, 32)
pta <- expand.grid(mic = mics, target = c(80, 48.46)) |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(pta = mean(fauc$fauc / mic >= target)) |>
  ungroup()

ggplot(pta, aes(mic, pta, colour = factor(target))) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  scale_x_log10(breaks = mics) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  labs(x = "MIC (mg/L)", y = "Probability of target attainment",
       colour = "fAUC0-24/MIC target",
       title = "Levofloxacin 750 mg once daily at steady state") +
  theme_minimal()
```

Applying the MIC distribution of Supplementary Table S3 (57 episodes at
32 mg/L, 3 at 16, 5 at 12, 3 at 6 and 35 at the 2 mg/L EUCAST ECOFF) to the
pooled cohort gives the overall attainment below, against the paper's 12/103
(11.7%) and 29/103 (28.2%).

```{r pta-overall}
mic_s3 <- c(rep(32, 57), rep(16, 3), rep(12, 5), rep(6, 3), rep(2, 35))
pta_overall <- sapply(c(80, 48.46), function(target) {
  mean(sapply(mic_s3, function(m) mean(fauc$fauc / m >= target)))
})
knitr::kable(
  data.frame(
    target = c("fAUC0-24/MIC >= 80", "fAUC0-24/MIC >= 48.46"),
    paper = c("12/103 (11.7%)", "29/103 (28.2%)"),
    simulated = sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * pta_overall)
  ) |>
    rename("Target" = target, "Bosnak 2026" = paper, "Simulated" = simulated),
  caption = "Overall target attainment with the Supplementary Table S3 MIC distribution."
)
```

Every attaining episode in the paper had the 2 mg/L ECOFF MIC (all colonizing
and clinical isolates had MICs of 6 mg/L or more, Supplementary Table S3, and
none of the 29 episodes attaining the 48.46 cutoff was colonized with
levofloxacin-resistant bacteria). The simulation assigns MICs to patients at
random, whereas the paper's ECOFF episodes are the patients with no positive
culture, a subgroup whose covariates are not published separately; the
simulated attainment is therefore a population-average figure and is expected
to fall below the paper's individual-level count. It is shown for orientation
and not used as a validation gate.

# Exposure-response findings not encoded

The paper's clinical analysis is a multivariable logistic regression of
prophylaxis failure on profound neutropenia (odds ratio 4.17) and on attaining
fAUC0-24/MIC >= 80 (odds ratio 0.12) or >= 48.46 (odds ratio 0.26). It is not
part of the packaged model: the drug term is a yes/no target-attainment
indicator rather than a continuous exposure, no intercept is reported, and in
a matched case-control design (failures matched one-to-one to successes) the
intercept reflects the sampling ratio rather than the risk of failure, so an
absolute probability of prophylaxis failure cannot be predicted from it.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **IIV scale.** Table 3 prints the between-subject variability as CV%. These
  are read as Monolix's log-normal coefficient of variation,
  `CV = sqrt(exp(omega^2) - 1)`, so `omega^2 = log(CV^2 + 1)` (0.1508 for
  CL/F, 0.1179 for V/F). Reading them as `100 * omega` would give 0.1628 and
  0.1251; the difference has no material effect on the comparisons above.
* **Bootstrap versus final estimates.** The final estimates of Table 3 are
  used; the bootstrap medians (for example IIV on V/F 29.1%) are reported in
  the in-file comments only.
* **Absorption rate constant.** Ka is fixed at 1.12 1/h, the preliminary
  estimate from model development, because sampling started at 2 h. The
  Results describe the expected Tmax as about 1.5 h; with Ka 1.12 1/h and the
  typical elimination rate the model's Tmax is about 2.9 h after a single dose,
  so concentrations in the first two hours are not informed by data.
* **Bioavailability.** Only oral data were collected, so CL/F and V/F are
  apparent and the model carries no bioavailability parameter, as in the
  authors' code.
* **Unbound AUC accumulator.** The authors' Monolix code integrates
  `0.7 * Cc` in an `fAUCtau` compartment that is a table output only. The
  packaged model exposes the unbound concentration `Cu` instead and leaves
  the integration to the user (here PKNCA), which gives the same quantity
  without an extra state.
* **Covariate cohort.** Cockcroft-Gault creatinine clearance is computed on
  total body weight because the paper does not name the weight. The group
  cohorts use the full 120-episode group summaries of Tables 1 and 2, because
  group summaries for the 103-episode PK set are not published.
* **Episodes, not patients.** The 120 neutropenic episodes came from 108
  patients; the analysis treated episodes as individuals, so the model's
  between-subject variability is between episodes.
